text:
sara_support: FYI — ACME reported a production spike of 504/5xx from /v1/rerank during their morning traffic bump. p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~2.3s, several customers retried and saw cascading 5xx. They provided a repro and sample payload.

jordan_cust: seeing this across multiple regions. Here’s a sanitized request: `POST /v1/rerank` payload: {
  "query": "best wireless earbuds 2025",
  "candidates": ["...200-item-array..."],
  "top_k": 5
}
We only started hitting it after increasing candidate_count to ~200.

mike_sre: tagging eng-runtime/eng-platform. Can we get traces/gateway logs + rerank service logs for the time window? Any recent canary or kernel changes?

sara_support: attach from ACME (timestamps 2026-03-16T08:12:22Z -> 08:17:03Z): gateway shows repeated 504s with backend upstream 502/503. Sample gateway entry: `gateway | 2026-03-16T08:14:00Z | 504 | req=abc123 | upstream=rerank-svc | attempt=3`

deploy-bot: (deploy) Canary rollout `rerank-runtime:v2.8.1` started 2026-03-15T23:40:12Z - progress 40% at 2026-03-16T07:00:00Z.

elaine_prodeng: noted. Customer's candidate count is high — we have heuristics that recommend <=128 candidates for rerank. Could be batching explosion. Can someone capture p95 p99 server-side for rerank during the window?

tom_backend: grabbing logs now. Initial quick check: rerank-service logs show timeouts from the scoring worker when candidate_count > 128; backend emitted `ERROR handler: scoring timeout after 15s | req=abc123 | candidates=200 | request_id=abc123`. Also seeing repeated retries from gateway causing concurrent inflight requests to spike. Kernel fallback warnings in the runtime: `kernel_select: fallback -> slow_scalar_path for model=xx, seq_len=256`

mike_sre: that matches a retry storm: client retries + gateway retries causing duplicate load. We should ask ACME to temporarily reduce client-side retries and lower candidate_count while we investigate. Also enabling per-route circuit breaker to 10s would help.

sara_support: communicated mitigations to ACME: 1) reduce candidate_count to <=64, 2) set exponential backoff with longer base (500ms -> 1s) on client retries, 3) include header `X-Redwood-Prefer-Fallback: true` if they can accept a cheaper model.

tom_backend: repro steps we used: 1) seed a request stream at 600 qps with payloads of 180 candidates 2) disable client retry deduplication 3) observe CPU/GPU kernel fallback and request queue growth -> scoring worker timeouts -> 502 -> gateway 504s. Sample load command: ```for i in {1..600}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/rerank -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"query":"x","candidates":["...180 items..."]}'; done```

elaine_prodeng: root cause candidate: batching algorithm created oversized fused batches for high candidate_count which force a non-optimized kernel path; when that happens per-request latency spikes and retries amplify the effect. There's also an edge bug where kernel selection fails to cap fused_batch_size for certain model quantization combos.

mike_sre: short-term mitigations we applied: 1) rollback canary to v2.8.0 (done 2026-03-16T08:45:12Z) 2) increased rerank dedicated pool autoscale limits for the zone serving ACME 3) added temporary route circuit-breaker: max_inflight=250, per-request timeout=10s. Early telemetry shows p95 falling back to ~200-300ms.

tom_backend: created PR #4245 with two fixes: a bounds-check on fused_batch_size and a fallback to split oversized candidate lists into sub-batches at the runtime layer. Hotfix merged to canary; will promote to stable after 2hr canary observation.

sara_support: ACME confirmed improvement after the suggested mitigations; they saw 504s stop and p95 drop to ~280ms. They will keep candidate_count <=100 for now.

elaine_prodeng: next steps: 1) merge + promote hotfix to stable if canary metrics hold 2) add a model/profile-level guard to reject requests with candidates > 512 (return 400 with helpful message) 3) update docs with recommended candidate limits and example efficient strategy (pre-filter + rerank top N) 4) build a routing rule to prefer cheaper model variants when candidate_count>128.

mike_sre: assigned follow-ups: tom_backend (runtime fix monitoring) + elaine_prodeng (policy + docs) + sara_support (customer comms closure).

jordan_cust: thanks team — appreciate the quick help and the suggested workarounds. Please keep us posted on the permanent fix timeline.

sara_support: will follow up after hotfix promotion and will post closure note. Closing interim owner: sara_support.

(attachments: gateway_logs_excerpt.txt, rerank_service_trace_20260316.json — attached to thread)
